options.timber_slab: Timber frame on a concrete slab
options.concrete_slab: Concrete or brick on a slab

options.control: Control (turn the switch on and off)

cop_degradation.title: Heat pump efficiency has dropped
cop_degradation.description: The heat pump has been delivering about {shortfall_percent} % less heat per kWh than it used to under the same conditions, which is costing roughly {cost_month} {currency} per month at recent prices. The usual suspects are a clogged filter, low refrigerant, or a defrost problem — worth a look before the season gets colder. This notice clears itself if efficiency recovers.

accuracy_drift.title: Learned model is drifting
accuracy_drift.description: The optimizer's predictions have been consistently off for several days, which usually means something about the house or the system changed faster than the learners can follow. Check that sensors read sensibly. If the plan has become noticeably worse, the "Restore learned snapshot" service rolls the learned model back to the last known-good weekly snapshot.

accuracy_drift_rolled_back.title: Learned model was restored from a snapshot
accuracy_drift_rolled_back.description: The optimizer's predictions drifted out of band for several days while all inputs looked healthy, so the learned model was automatically rolled back to the most recent known-good weekly snapshot. Nothing is required from you; this notice is here so the change is visible. If the drift was real — new radiators, changed insulation — the learners will simply relearn from the restored point.

freq_watchdog.title: Frequency control stood down
freq_watchdog.description: The compressor frequency reported by {entity} kept diverging from the commanded value, so frequency control fell back to observe mode and no further writes will be made. This usually means the wrong register or entity is configured, or the pump is in a protective mode that ignores external commands. Check the entity, then re-arm by switching the frequency mode to observe, saving, and switching back to control.

solve_failures.title: Optimization keeps failing; the plan is going stale
solve_failures.description: The last {count} optimization runs failed, so the integration is still showing — and until recently acting on — a plan computed at {last_success}. Once the plan is older than a few update intervals the heat pump is handed back to its own heating curve rather than driven from an outdated schedule. The usual suspects are a lost price or weather connection, or an error in the log from the solver itself. This notice clears on the next successful optimization.

solve_worker_fallback.title: Planning fell back to the slow in-process solver
solve_worker_fallback.description: The separate solver process could not be used, so the optimization ran inside Home Assistant's own interpreter instead. The plan is correct, but the solve holds the interpreter lock while it runs, so Home Assistant may feel briefly unresponsive on each optimization. The cause reported was: {cause}. Please attach that line and the log to a report. This notice clears once a solve completes in the separate process again.

pump_mode_unreadable.title: Heat pump operating mode entity is not reporting
pump_mode_unreadable.description: The entity you chose for the heat pump's operating mode has not been readable for over {hours} hours. The last mode it reported was “{mode}”, and until now the plan was still being held to what that mode can deliver. It has stopped being held to it: an operating mode nobody has been able to read for hours is no longer evidence about what the pump is doing, and continuing to suppress heating or hot water on it would leave you cold on the word of a dead sensor. The plan is back to assuming the pump can do everything, which is what it assumed before you configured this entity. Check that the entity still exists and is available, or clear the slot if you no longer want it used. This notice clears as soon as the entity reports again.

dhw_disinfection_switch_lost.title: The pump's disinfection switch may still be on
dhw_disinfection_switch_lost.description: The optimizer turned on {entity_id} for a disinfection cycle, but that switch has not been readable for half an hour — it may have been renamed, removed or replaced in these settings — so the optimizer can no longer turn it off and has stopped trying. Check the heat pump's own disinfection switch and turn it off if it is still on. If you renamed it, turn it off by hand before choosing the new entity on the hot water tank settings page: the optimizer only ever turns off a switch it turned on itself, so it leaves a switch that is already on alone.

dhw_disinfection_write_failed.title: The pump's disinfection switch could not be set
dhw_disinfection_write_failed.description: The anti-legionella cycle tried to set {entity_id}, and Home Assistant refused the call, so the pump's own disinfection program may not be running when the plan expects it to. The write is retried on every update, and this notice clears itself as soon as one goes through. Check that the entity exists and is available, or set the disinfection switch mode back to observe.

dhw_legionella_mode_blocked.title: Hot water disinfection is overdue: the heat pump's mode blocks it
dhw_legionella_mode_blocked.description: The anti-legionella cycle was due {overdue_days} day(s) ago, but the heat pump reports an operating mode that makes no hot water at all, so the plan has nowhere to put the cycle and is not scheduling it. Nothing is being changed on your behalf: hot water is never planned into a mode the pump cannot serve, because that would promise water the hardware refuses to heat. The tank is simply not being disinfected while the pump stays in this mode. Switch the pump to a mode that includes hot water, or turn the disinfection cycle off if that is deliberate. It normally runs every {interval_days} days, and this notice clears as soon as a cycle can be planned again.

dhw_legionella_unreachable.title: Hot water is not reaching the disinfection temperature
dhw_legionella_unreachable.description: The anti-legionella cycle ran, but the tank only reached {reached} °C against the {target} °C it was asked for, so the water is not being disinfected. Heat pumps often cannot get a tank that hot on their own; the usual answer is an immersion heater that takes the last few degrees, or lowering the disinfection temperature to something this system can actually hold. Until then the cycle will be retried once per interval rather than on every plan. This notice clears itself as soon as a cycle reaches temperature.

dhw_legionella_unverified.title: The disinfection cycle cannot be verified
dhw_legionella_unverified.description: The anti-legionella cycle was commanded, but no hot water tank temperature sensor is configured, so nothing confirms the tank ever reached {target} °C — or that the pump acted on the request at all. The countdown is reset as if the cycle had run, because refusing to reset it would not disinfect anything either; what is not claimed is that it worked. Point the "Hot water tank temperature" sensor at a real probe and the cycle is verified from then on, and this notice clears as soon as one is observed at temperature.

dhw_legionella_above_setpoint.title: Disinfection goes above your hot water charge limit
dhw_legionella_above_setpoint.description: The anti-legionella cycle is set to {legionella_temp} °C, which is above the {setpoint} °C you set as the highest tank temperature to charge to. That is allowed and nothing is wrong: every {interval_days} days the tank is taken up to {legionella_temp} °C for the cycle, and the rest of the time it is never charged above {setpoint} °C. This notice is here so the one hot day a week does not come as a surprise. Raise the charge limit, lower the disinfection temperature, or switch the cycle off to change it.

grid_fee_magnitude.title: A configured grid fee looks 100× too large
grid_fee_magnitude.description: The grid fee layer contains a rate of {rate} {currency}/kWh (from the {source} input). Transfer fees run a few tenths of a {currency} per kWh, so a value this size is almost always öre or cents entered where whole {currency} were meant — 25 instead of 0.25. Nothing is changed or capped: the plan keeps pricing with exactly the value configured. Correct the value under the DSO fee options (or fix the fee sensor) and this notice clears on the next planning cycle.

grid_fee_sign.title: A configured grid fee is negative
grid_fee_sign.description: The grid fee layer contains a rate of {rate} {currency}/kWh (from the {source} input). A transfer fee is a charge, so a negative one is almost always a sign slip — and the plan is pricing every hour it applies to as subsidised, favouring exactly the hours the grid company charges for. Nothing is changed or capped: the plan keeps pricing with exactly the value configured. Correct the value under the DSO fee options (or fix the fee sensor) and this notice clears on the next planning cycle.

lower_floor_modelled.title: The downstairs temperature is modelled, not measured
lower_floor_modelled.description: Two-zone planning is on and no lower-floor thermometer is configured, so the lower zone starts from the main room sensor and is carried forward by the thermal model — the “Lower floor (modelled)” trace on the plan chart. That is how the zone has to be planned without a sensor, and it is not something the floor-return sensor can supply: return water runs 3–9 K above the room it heats, so it drives the slab estimate, which is what it is genuinely a proxy for. What a modelled zone cannot do is correct itself, so over a long cold spell it can drift from the real downstairs. Assigning “Lower floor temperature sensor” under the zone options closes that loop; this notice clears when you do.

comfort_band_contradiction.title: Your comfort temperatures contradict each other
comfort_band_contradiction.description: The stored comfort settings cannot all be satisfied at once: {problem}. Until version 5.1.7 the thermostat card's temperature slider ran one degree past the warmest acceptable temperature and saved whatever it was given, so a single tap on its top notch could store a target above the ceiling. Nothing is broken — the optimizer prices these bounds rather than enforcing them, so the plan keeps running, just in permanent slight violation of a band it can never satisfy. Nothing has been changed for you either: which of the two numbers is the wrong one is yours to say. Correct them under the temperature options and this notice clears on the next cycle.

dhw_setpoint_below_disinfection.title: The heat pump's hot water set-point is below the configured temperature

fix_flow.flow_title: Raise the heat pump's hot water set-point

confirm.title: Set the pump to {target} °C
confirm.description: The pump's DHW set-point on {entity} is below {target} °C. This writes {target} °C to that entity, the disinfection or minimum temperature already configured.

space_setpoint_unreadable.title: The space-heating set-point entity is not reporting
space_setpoint_unreadable.description: The entity you chose as the space-heating set-point ({entity}) is missing or unreadable, so nothing can be said about the pump's current target. The space-heating set-point is never recommended; this notice only reports that the entity cannot be read. Check that it still exists and is available, or clear the slot. This notice clears as soon as the entity reports a temperature.

state.dhw_preheat: Charging the tank while electricity is cheap
state.pump_mode: Blocked by the heat pump's mode

run_optimization.name: Run Optimization
run_optimization.description: Manually trigger the heat pump cost optimization. This will fetch the latest electricity prices and weather forecast, then compute the optimal heat pump schedule for the next 24 hours using predictive MPC with solar/wind/rain anticipation and DHW coordination. The call fails with an error when the optimization cannot run — for example fewer than four electricity price steps are available, or the solve failed — instead of returning as if a new plan had been computed.

set_away.name: Set Away
set_away.description: Turn the Plan-page away override on or off, and optionally set or clear the expected return time. At least one field is required. Turning the override off also clears the return time.

active.name: Away
active.description: Turn the override on or off. Omit to leave on/off unchanged.

return_time.name: Expected return
return_time.description: ISO datetime, or empty to clear. Omit to leave the stored time. Setting a time while the override is off stores it without turning away on.

set_mode.name: Set Optimizer Mode
set_mode.description: Set the operating mode of the heat pump optimizer.

mode.name: Mode
mode.description:
The operating mode to set. Available modes: - auto: Full MPC optimization with predictive weather anticipation (recommended) - comfort: Maintain comfort temperature, ignore price optimization - economy: Lets the plan take the house up to 1.5 °C below your
  comfort floor to ride out expensive hours (never below 15 °C)
- boost: Maximum heating power - off: Disable optimizer, heat pump left in default state

set_thermal_parameters.name: Set Thermal Parameters
set_thermal_parameters.description: Update the thermal model parameters used by the optimizer. Useful for fine-tuning the model to match your house's actual thermal behavior. Supports single-zone, two-zone, DHW, and weather sensitivity parameters.

house_thermal_mass.name: House Thermal Mass
house_thermal_mass.description: Thermal mass of the house (air + furnishings) in kWh/°C. Higher values mean slower temperature changes. Roughly 0.02 kWh/°C per m² of heated area for a timber house; heavy floors are counted under slab_thermal_mass instead.

house_heat_loss_coefficient.name: Heat Loss Coefficient
house_heat_loss_coefficient.description: Overall heat loss coefficient in kW/°C. Lower values indicate better insulation.

slab_thermal_mass.name: Slab Thermal Mass
slab_thermal_mass.description: Thermal mass of whatever the heat is delivered through, in kWh/°C: the concrete slab of a floor-heated house, or the water and steel of a radiator circuit, which is far smaller.

slab_heat_transfer.name: Slab Heat Transfer Coefficient
slab_heat_transfer.description: Heat transfer coefficient between that store and the room, in kW/°C. Radiators sit far higher than a slab.

heat_pump_cop_nominal.name: Heat Pump Nominal COP
heat_pump_cop_nominal.description: Nominal COP of the heat pump at 7°C outdoor temperature.

upper_floor_thermal_mass.name: Upper Floor Thermal Mass
upper_floor_thermal_mass.description: Thermal mass of the upper floor (radiator zone) in kWh/°C.

lower_floor_thermal_mass.name: Lower Floor Thermal Mass
lower_floor_thermal_mass.description: Thermal mass of the lower floor (slab zone) in kWh/°C.

inter_zone_heat_transfer.name: Inter-Zone Heat Transfer
inter_zone_heat_transfer.description: Heat transfer coefficient between upper and lower floors in kW/°C. Higher values for open floor plans.

radiator_power_fraction.name: Radiator Power Fraction
radiator_power_fraction.description: Fraction of heat pump output going to radiators (upper floor). 0.0 = all floor heating, 1.0 = all radiators.

window_area.name: Window Area
window_area.description: Total glazing area for solar heat gain calculation in m².

solar_heat_gain_coefficient.name: Solar Heat Gain Coefficient (SHGC)
solar_heat_gain_coefficient.description: Fraction of solar energy transmitted through windows. Typical values: 0.3 (triple low-e) to 0.8 (single clear).

dhw_tank_volume.name: DHW Tank Volume
dhw_tank_volume.description: Volume of the domestic hot water storage tank in liters.

dhw_setpoint.name: DHW Setpoint Temperature
dhw_setpoint.description: Target temperature for the domestic hot water tank in °C.

dhw_min_temperature.name: DHW Minimum Temperature
dhw_min_temperature.description: Minimum acceptable DHW tank temperature in °C, enforced during the configured hot water time frames.

dhw_daily_consumption.name: DHW Daily Consumption
dhw_daily_consumption.description: Estimated daily hot water consumption in liters/day.

dhw_cooling_rate.name: DHW Tank Cooling Rate
dhw_cooling_rate.description: How fast the tank cools with no draw, in °C per hour at 45 °C tank temperature and 20 °C ambient. Normally learned automatically from observed standby decay; set it to seed or override the learned value.

buffer_cooling_rate.name: Buffer Tank Cooling Rate
buffer_cooling_rate.description: How fast the buffer tank cools with the pump off, in °C per hour at 25 °C above ambient. Learned automatically when a buffer tank temperature sensor is configured; setting it here reseeds the learned value and resets the sample count.

dhw_schedule_enabled.name: DHW Time Frames Enabled
dhw_schedule_enabled.description: When on, hot water is only guaranteed during the configured time frames. When off, hot water is required around the clock.

dhw_windows.name: DHW Demand Time Frames
dhw_windows.description: Time frames when hot water must be available, as 24-hour times separated by commas. Frames may wrap past midnight. Leave empty to derive them from the learned usage profile. Unparseable frames are rejected, not silently ignored.

dhw_idle_min_temperature.name: DHW Idle Minimum Temperature
dhw_idle_min_temperature.description: Lowest tank temperature the optimizer will plan for outside the demand time frames.

dhw_legionella_enabled.name: Anti-Legionella Cycle
dhw_legionella_enabled.description: Periodically heat the tank to the disinfection temperature.

dhw_legionella_temperature.name: Anti-Legionella Temperature
dhw_legionella_temperature.description: Tank temperature reached during an anti-legionella cycle.

dhw_legionella_interval_days.name: Anti-Legionella Interval
dhw_legionella_interval_days.description: Maximum number of days between anti-legionella cycles.

wind_sensitivity_factor.name: Wind Sensitivity Factor
wind_sensitivity_factor.description: How much wind increases heat loss. 0.15 means 15% more heat loss per m/s of wind speed. Adjusts convective heat transfer.

rain_heat_loss_multiplier.name: Rain Heat Loss Multiplier
rain_heat_loss_multiplier.description: Heat loss multiplier when raining. 1.15 means 15% more heat loss during rain (wet building envelope effect).

ecl110_pid_time_constant_hours.name: ECL110 PI/PID Time Constant
ecl110_pid_time_constant_hours.description: Time constant (hours) for the ECL110 PI/PID response approximation. Lower values react faster, higher values are smoother.

ecl110_displace_min.name: ECL110 displace minimum
ecl110_displace_min.description: Lowest parallel shift the optimizer may command, in °C.

ecl110_displace_max.name: ECL110 displace maximum
ecl110_displace_max.description: Highest parallel shift the optimizer may command, in °C.

simulate_plan.name: Simulate a plan
simulate_plan.description: Price a hypothetical comfort choice against the current forecast without disturbing operation. Returns the cost difference against the live plan. Backs the dashboard card's what-if simulator; the underlying solve is rate-limited, so rapid repeat calls return the previous answer. A what-if that cannot run — no plan yet, not enough price data, unparseable hot water windows — fails with an error rather than an error entry inside the response.

min_temp.name: Minimum temperature
min_temp.description: Lowest acceptable temperature to test, in °C.

max_temp.name: Maximum temperature
max_temp.description: Highest acceptable temperature to test, in °C.

comfort_weight.name: Comfort weight
comfort_weight.description: How hard to chase price versus hold temperature.

comfort_temp_day.name: Daytime comfort temperature
comfort_temp_day.description: Comfort temperature during the heating day, in °C.

comfort_temp_night.name: Night comfort temperature
comfort_temp_night.description: Comfort temperature outside the heating day, in °C.

dhw_min_temperature.name: Hot water minimum
dhw_min_temperature.description: Usable minimum inside demand windows, in °C.

day_start_hour.name: Heating day starts
day_start_hour.description: Hour at which the daytime comfort temperature takes over from the night one.

day_end_hour.name: Heating day ends
day_end_hour.description: Hour at which the night setback begins.

dhw_windows.name: Hot water demand windows
dhw_windows.description: Time frames to test, e.g. "06:00-08:30, 17:00-22:00". An empty string simulates having no demand windows at all.

wood_slots.name: Wood slots
wood_slots.description: What-if wood fires as a list of objects each carrying a start, an end and a volume in liters. Injected only into the shadow solve; never written to the config entry.

wood_type.name: Wood type
wood_type.description: What-if wood type override (birch, pine, mixed).

wood_price_sek_m3.name: Wood price
wood_price_sek_m3.description: What-if firewood price in SEK per billed cubic metre.

assign_entity.name: Assign Entity
assign_entity.description: Assign one of the integration's optional sensors, or clear it. This is what the setup diagram on the dashboard card calls when you click a slot, and it writes the same configuration the options pages write. Changing the configuration reloads the integration.

key.name: Setting
key.description: Which optional sensor to assign, by its configuration key - for example buffer_tank_temp_entity.

entity_id.name: Entity
entity_id.description: The entity to assign. Leave empty to clear the slot. The entity must exist and its domain must be one the slot accepts.

entry_id.name: Config entry
entry_id.description: Restrict the change to one heat pump. Omit to apply to all of them.

manual_setpoint.name: Manual setpoint
manual_setpoint.description: The indoor temperature the valve holds when no target sensor is assigned. Leave at 0 to use the top of the comfort band. Ignored for any other slot.

apply_topology.name: Apply Topology Layout
apply_topology.description: Store the hydronic layout the setup diagram's editor snapped to, plus the cosmetic box positions. Only layouts from the supported catalog are accepted, and only when this system's configuration can honor them — a two-tank layout needs a wood-tank probe, a valved layout needs a valve. Changing the configuration reloads the integration.

layout.name: Layout
layout.description: The catalog key of the layout - for example two_tank_4way or valve_upper_direct_slab.

positions.name: Box positions
positions.description: Cosmetic diagram positions, as a mapping from place name to [x, y]. Never affects the physics.

entry_id.name: Config entry
entry_id.description: Restrict the change to one heat pump. Omit to apply to all of them.

dhw.name: DHW tank
dhw.description: When set, add or remove the domestic hot water tank from this system's picture. True seeds a default volume if none is stored yet. Omit to leave the tank as it is.

wood.name: Wood tank
wood.description: When set, add or remove the wood / external-heat tank from this system's picture. Omit to leave the tank as it is.

apply_schedule.name: Apply Schedule
apply_schedule.description: Save a heating and hot water schedule into the integration's configuration, so the optimizer plans against it from now on. This is the deliberate counterpart to simulate_plan, which only prices a schedule without keeping it. Changing the configuration reloads the integration.

day_start_hour.name: Heating day starts
day_start_hour.description: Hour at which the daytime comfort temperature takes over from the night one.

day_end_hour.name: Heating day ends
day_end_hour.description: Hour at which the night setback begins.

dhw_windows.name: Hot water demand windows
dhw_windows.description: Time frames when hot water must be available, e.g. "06:00-08:30, 17:00-22:00". An empty string removes all demand windows, leaving the tank only at its idle minimum.

comfort_temp_day.name: Daytime comfort temperature
comfort_temp_day.description: Target indoor temperature during the heating day.

dhw_min_temperature.name: Minimum hot water temperature
dhw_min_temperature.description: Lowest tank temperature considered usable inside a demand window. It must stay a few degrees below the hot water setpoint, or the tank would have to sit exactly at target and the pump would short-cycle; a value that leaves no deadband is rejected.

entry_id.name: Config entry
entry_id.description: Restrict the change to one config entry. Leave empty to apply to every configured heat pump, which is what a single-heat-pump install wants.

apply_manual_plan.name: Apply Manual Plan
apply_manual_plan.description: Pin exactly when space heating and hot water run for the next 20 hours. Unlike apply_schedule, which only shifts the envelope the optimizer keeps re-deciding inside, this fixes the actual run slots until the override expires. Safety still wins: if the tank falls below its minimum, a legionella cycle is due, or the house drops below its comfort floor, the pinned-off slot is released and the system runs anyway.

space_slots.name: Space heating slots
space_slots.description: When space heating should run, as a list of objects each carrying a start and an end as ISO 8601 datetimes. An empty list forces space heating off for the whole period; omit the field entirely to leave space heating fully automatic.

dhw_slots.name: Hot water slots
dhw_slots.description: When hot water should run, as a list of objects each carrying a start and an end as ISO 8601 datetimes. An empty list forces hot water off for the whole period; omit the field entirely to leave hot water fully automatic.

expires_at.name: Expires at
expires_at.description: ISO 8601 datetime when the override stops applying and planning reverts to automatic. Defaults to 20 hours from now, restarted each time you apply. It is deliberately shorter than the optimizer's 24-hour horizon, so there is always a tail the optimizer still owns.

entry_id.name: Config entry
entry_id.description: Restrict the override to one config entry. Leave empty to apply to every configured heat pump.

clear_manual_plan.name: Clear Manual Plan
clear_manual_plan.description: Remove any manual plan override immediately, so planning reverts to fully automatic.

entry_id.name: Config entry
entry_id.description: Restrict the clear to one config entry. Leave empty to clear every configured heat pump.

restore_learned_snapshot.name: Restore Learned Snapshot
restore_learned_snapshot.description: Roll every learner back to the most recent weekly snapshot that was captured while all inputs were healthy and prediction accuracy was in band. Use this if the learned model has visibly gone wrong — after a sensor fed garbage for a while, for example. The drift watchdog does the same thing automatically when it can prove the inputs were healthy throughout; this service is the manual override for when you can see what it cannot. Nothing is lost permanently: learning simply continues from the restored point. The call fails with an error when no snapshot qualifies, instead of answering with an empty restore.

entry_id.name: Config entry
entry_id.description: Restrict the restore to one config entry. Leave empty to restore every configured heat pump.

diagnose_interval.name: Diagnose Last Interval
diagnose_interval.description: Explain the last interval's temperature error, input by input. The optimizer re-runs the interval that just settled through its own thermal model, swapping one realised input at a time into the plan's assumptions — measured power for commanded power, realised outdoor temperature for the forecast, realised solar for the assumed — and reports how much of the error each swap explains. What no swap explains is the model's own residual, reported as "unexplained". The result is published on the Prediction Accuracy sensor and returned as the service response.

entry_id.name: Config entry
entry_id.description: Restrict the diagnosis to one config entry. Leave empty to diagnose every configured heat pump.
